mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team B being a low-shots-conceded opponent (season mean shots-against well below competition context mean). Within that condition, examine whether Team A's shots-to-shots-on-target ratio and shots-on-target-to-goals ratio jointly differ from their unconditional season averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-on-target rate and goals-per-shot-on-target are suppressed when facing a low-shots-conceding opponent, even as raw shot volume remains elevated — i.e., volume does not linearly predict on-target or goal output against such opponents.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its conversion to goals has declined in recent matches, while Team B concedes very few shots against. The joint relationship between Team A's shots-for and its shots-on-target-for, conditioned on Team B's shots-against suppression level, tests whether high shot volume translates to on-target output when facing a low-shots-conceding opponent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint three-variable relationship (shots, shots_on_target, goals) conditioned simultaneously on the opponent's shots-against level. It is not reducible to any single observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart, nor to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams having above-competition-average shots-for. Within this two-sided high-volume condition, examine whether shots-on-target and goals outcomes for each side differ from single-team baselines — specifically testing whether the interaction of two high-volume attacking teams compresses or amplifies on-target rates.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams produce above-average shot volumes, the shots-on-target rate per shot is suppressed relative to single-team baselines, reflecting defensive pressure from both sides; goals outcomes do not scale linearly with combined shot volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B produces a high shots volume relative to the competition context but concedes very few shots. The asymmetric relationship between Team B's shots-for and Team A's shots-against (both relative to competition baseline) tests whether a dominant-possession, high-shot-volume attacker facing a high-shot-volume opponent produces a different shots-on-target and goals outcome than when facing a low-shot-volume opponent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint two-team, two-observable interaction (both teams' shots-for simultaneously above baseline) conditioned on a second observable (shots-on-target), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: Team A's goals-against first-half vs second-half, and Team B's goals-for first-half vs second-half. Test whether the joint half-level distribution (both teams' tendencies combined) differs from what either team's individual half split would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half is disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half in this matchup, beyond what either team's individual half-split tendency would predict alone — i.e., the two half-level tendencies reinforce each other.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes a high volume of goals in the first half relative to the second half, while Team B scores more in the second half than the first. The joint within-match half-level goal distribution for both teams tests whether the combination of Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability and Team B's second-half attacking tendency produces a distinctive half-level goals pattern in this matchup.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct within-match half-level splits for two different teams across an asymmetric observable (goals-against for Team A, goals-for for Team B), which is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split for both teams simultaneously: Team A's corners-for first-half vs second-half, and Team B's corners-for first-half vs second-half. Test whether the combined half-level corner distribution differs from what each team's individual half split predicts in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner production shifts across halves in opposing directions for the two teams — Team A dominates corners in the first half while Team B's corner share rises in the second half — producing a non-uniform intra-match corner timing pattern that is not captured by full-match corner totals alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more corners in the first half than the second half, while Team B generates more corners in the second half than the first. The joint within-match half-level corner distribution tests whether the two teams' opposing half-level corner tendencies produce a distinctive intra-match corner timing pattern — specifically whether the first half is corner-dominated by Team A and the second half by Team B.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' within-match half-level splits for the same observable (corners), examining the interaction of opposing half-level tendencies. This is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level trend.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams having above-competition-average possession (indicating a contested possession match). Within this condition, examine whether fouls-for and yellow-cards-for are elevated or suppressed relative to each team's unconditional averages, and whether second-half cards (cards_2h) are disproportionately elevated relative to full-match yellow cards.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In contested high-possession matchups, fouls and second-half cards rise relative to each team's unconditional averages, and the second-half card share of total cards is elevated — reflecting increased contest intensity as both teams press for possession control in the closing stages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession is substantially above competition average while Team B also holds above-average possession. The joint relationship between both teams' possession levels and their respective foul rates tests whether high-possession matchups (where both teams compete for ball control) produce a different fouls-per-match and cards-in-second-half pattern than matchups where possession is more asymmetric.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint four-variable relationship (possession, fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) conditioned on both teams simultaneously exceeding a possession threshold, and further examines the within-match temporal distribution (second-half cards vs full-match cards). This is not reducible to any single observable mirror or single-band conditioning.
